24 Et. Gen. (AB) ἐκυδάασσατο: it means 'he reviled'. I 1337. And it is κύδος... Aesch. Prom. 714 Xen. An. V 5, 1 Strab. XII 549 Dion. Per. 768 with Eust. comm. Steph. Byz. Χάλυβες sch. Lyc. 1109 Ps.-Arist. De mirab. ausc. 48 Amm. Marc. XXII 8, 21
'He is reviled by all the Argives together'.

In the masculine and among the Syracusans it means 'abuse'. Therefore from κῦδος comes κυδάζω, κυδάζομαι, κυδάζεται; and Sophocles in Ajax the Whip-bearer: 'he is reviled by all the Argives' instead of 'he is abused'. Hesych. Phot. Suid. κῦδος Hesych. Phot. κυδάζεσθαι Suid. κυδάζεται Eust. 64, 31. 790, 40
